description:
Project: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration

Goal
Wire Redwood’s rollout controller (canary + A/B testing + staged model deployments) to latency and error-rate SLO monitors so the platform can automatically rollback (or pause) a rollout when an SLO breach is detected, using configurable thresholds per route/model/region/customer tier.

Why now (company context)
Redwood Inference differentiates on production reliability and predictable latency for LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. As traffic grows and more customers run aggressive rollouts, manual mitigation during latency/error regressions is too slow and risks SLA violations. This project turns SLO monitoring into an automated safety rail for model lifecycle operations in the Console and control plane.

Scope
- Rollout controller integration:
  - Subscribe to SLO monitors (p95/p99 latency, error rate, saturation signals where relevant) for the exact scope of a rollout (service/route, model version, region, customer tier).
  - Define breach evaluation logic: burn-rate/windows (e.g., 5m fast burn + 30m slow burn), minimum sample sizes, holdoff/debounce, and “do not rollback during known incident” overrides.
  - Actions: automatic rollback to last known-good version, pause rollout at current step, or shift traffic back to baseline (A/B) depending on policy.
  - Auditability: record reason, metrics snapshot, and decision trace; expose in Console and logs.

- Policy + configuration:
  - Per-rollout and per-service defaults with safe bounds (guardrails to prevent oscillation).
  - Integration with existing policy engine / config service.

- Observability:
  - Standard metric names and labels for rollouts + SLO evaluation outcomes.
  - Dashboards + alerts for “auto-rollback triggered”, “rollback suppressed”, and “monitor missing / stale”.

- Reliability/Operations:
  - Runbooks for on-call: how to interpret auto-rollback events, how to override, how to re-attempt rollout after fix.
  - Game day / incident simulations validating rollback behavior.

Non-goals (initial release)
- Fully autonomous multi-region failover orchestration (beyond rollback/pause).
- Quality/regression eval-based rollback (handled separately under eval/guardrails; can be added later as another signal).

Stakeholders / teams
- Product: Marissa Cole (Dir Product, Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (PM for rollout policies)
- Engineering: Chloe Martin + Jada Williams (Console backend + rollouts), Benji Okafor + Jordan Lee (control plane/policy engine)
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello
- Release/QA: Connor O’Brien (release eng), Leila Farouk (E2E automation)

High-level timeline (example)
1) Discovery + design (2–3 weeks): PRD, policy model, monitor semantics, failure modes/guardrails, initial UI/UX needs.
2) Implementation (4–6 weeks): controller hooks, policy evaluation, monitor adapters, audit trail, dashboards.
3) Hardening (2–3 weeks): load tests, canary on internal services, game day, runbook finalization.
4) Launch (1–2 weeks): staged enablement by environment/region, customer tier gating, post-launch review.

Key deliverables
- Confluence PRD + engineering design + ADRs
- Linear project plan (epics + tasks)
- GitHub PR series implementing controller integration, policy config, metrics/dashboards
- SRE runbooks + dashboards
- Slack coordination threads and incident-style simulations
- Optional customer-driven artifacts (support ticket + CRM notes) motivating requirements

files.description: Product requirements doc: user goals (SRE + platform engineers), rollout states/actions, policy configuration UX expectations, default thresholds, safety guardrails, phased rollout plan, and success metrics (reduced MTTR, fewer SLA breaches).

Engineering design spec: architecture diagram (text), monitor data flow, evaluation windows, minimum sample rules, action decision tree (pause vs rollback), data model changes, API endpoints, and backward compatibility.
ADR documenting chosen breach evaluation strategy (burn-rate/windows, debounce/holdoff, sample-size gating), alternatives considered, and rationale to avoid rollback oscillation.
ADR defining audit event schema for auto-rollback/pause decisions: required fields (metrics snapshot refs, monitor ids, policy version, acting service), retention, and privacy constraints.
Observability standard: canonical metric names/labels for rollout steps, evaluated SLOs, decision outcomes, and suppression reasons; includes cardinality guidance.
Service doc for the rollout controller: responsibilities, dependencies (policy engine, telemetry, monitor provider), failure modes, and ownership/oncall notes.
SRE doc defining which SLOs are eligible signals for rollback (latency p95/p99, error rate, saturation), recommended thresholds by tier, and guidance for new services/models.
Runbook: how to triage an auto-rollback event, verify monitor correctness, identify culprit deploy/model, override/suppress rollback, and safely restart the rollout.
Incident playbook section describing when to rely on auto-rollback vs manual actions, comms expectations, and escalation paths if rollback fails or worsens the incident.
Reliability initiative page: target top incident classes (latency regressions during rollouts), milestones, metrics (MTTR, rollback time), and cross-team responsibilities.
Release engineering notes on adding checks/gates (e.g., required dashboards/monitors present) before enabling auto-rollback for a new service/model.
Postmortem for a simulated/real rollout latency regression: where auto-rollback didn’t trigger (monitor missing/stale), corrective actions that directly feed this project.
Working doc brainstorming policy UX and semantics: per-rollout overrides, default templates, ‘pause vs rollback’ toggles, suppression windows, and open questions for PM/Eng.
Engineering notes: early architecture sketches, integration points with policy engine, monitor adapter interface draft, and a list of edge cases discovered during spike.
Spreadsheet-like doc: current SLO monitor coverage by service/route/region, gaps, owners, and which monitors are ‘safe’ to be used as auto-rollback signals.
Game day plan: scenarios (latency spike, 5xx burst, monitor staleness), expected controller behavior, success criteria, and rollback/suppression validation steps.
Console working notes describing the UI for showing auto actions: timeline view, links to dashboards, ‘why did we rollback’ explanation, and admin-only controls.
Rollout plan for the feature itself: dev/staging/prod phases, internal canary services, region-by-region enablement, and backout criteria.
Checklist of failure modes: metric lag, partial outages of telemetry, false positives, traffic shifts; proposed guardrails like minimum volume + dual-window confirmation.
Runtime team input: which latency percentiles and breakdown dimensions are meaningful, how tail latency behaves under batching changes, and recommended alert windows.
Draft customer-facing explanation (internal): what auto-rollback means, how thresholds are chosen, what customers will see in Console, and limitations.
PR to add an SLO evaluator hook to the rollout controller: wiring, feature flag, and initial decision outcomes (pause only) with unit tests.
PR adding policy schema for auto-rollback thresholds, windows, and suppression settings; includes validation and safe bounds.
PR to expose auto-rollback events via Console backend API endpoints, including pagination and filtering by rollout id and time window.
PR emitting structured audit events for auto decisions (rollback/pause/suppress), including correlation ids and links to monitor definitions.
PR implementing rollback execution for canary/A-B traffic splits with safeguards (rate-limited shifts, step-down strategy, idempotency).
PR adding adapter to query SLO monitor provider (internal toolkit): fetch burn-rate status, sample sizes, and timestamps; handles staleness.
PR implementing debounce/holdoff and minimum request-volume requirements; includes simulation tests to avoid flapping.
PR adding metrics for evaluation outcomes and decisions; includes label/cardinality constraints and examples for dashboards.
PR adding Grafana dashboards + alert rules for auto-rollback triggers, suppressions, monitor staleness, and per-service rollout health views.
PR in slo-toolkit to support querying burn-rate by rollout scope (model version/route/region), including caching and query efficiency improvements.
PR updating incident-bot to post a concise Slack notification when an auto-rollback occurs, with links to dashboards and rollout id.
PR adding end-to-end tests in staging: inject synthetic latency/error signals, verify controller pauses/rolls back, and verify audit trail + UI surfaces.
PR discovered during integration: fixes a race in step transitions that could cause double-execution of rollback; adds locking/idempotency guard.
PR adding admin-only override APIs: temporarily suppress auto rollback for a rollout/service with justification recorded in audit log.
PR updating internal docs site references and linking to Confluence runbook/standards; includes examples of policy config JSON.
PM ticket defining MVP scope, requirements, non-goals, and launch criteria; includes links to PRD/design spec and customer-impact assessment.
PM ticket specifying default thresholds by tier (self-serve/dedicated/private), recommended evaluation windows, and template names shown in Console.
Engineering ticket for controller integration hook, feature flag strategy, and acceptance tests.
Engineering ticket: implement config schema + validation + migration plan for existing rollout policies.
Engineering ticket: implement SLO query adapter, staleness handling, and caching requirements.
Engineering ticket: ensure rollback actions are idempotent, rate-limited, and safe under partial failures.
Engineering ticket: expose auto-rollback events via Console backend APIs, include filtering and RBAC considerations.
Engineering ticket for UI work: show auto actions with ‘why’ details and links to dashboards/metrics.
Engineering ticket adding standard metrics + ensuring label/cardinality compliance.
Engineering ticket (owned by obs/SRE) to ship alert rules and route notifications to correct Slack channels/oncall.
QA/E2E ticket: simulate latency/error spikes, verify pause/rollback behavior, verify audit trail and suppression controls.
Release engineering ticket: staged rollout plan, enablement flags, and backout playbook for the feature itself.
SRE ticket to produce/runbook updates and ensure oncall readiness; includes training items and links to dashboards.
Engineering ticket: implement minimum sample sizes + debounce rules and document rationale.
Engineering ticket implementing suppression windows and admin override flow; requires audit logging.
Engineering ticket updating incident-bot integration and message formatting; ensures no paging storms.
SRE ticket planning and executing a game day; captures findings and follow-ups.
Design ticket for Console UI: event detail panel (metrics snapshot summary, decision explanation, action buttons), including edge cases (missing monitor, suppressed).
Design ticket for policy editor: thresholds, windows, templates, inline warnings, and safe defaults UX.
Thread coordinating the initial spike: where to hook SLO evaluation into the rollout state machine; includes @mentions of Console + control plane engineers.
Thread debating default thresholds/windows and how to avoid flapping; SRE shares historical incident examples and recommended burn-rate patterns.
Thread on architecture review: whether evaluation happens in controller vs dedicated service; discussion of failure modes and consistency guarantees.
Thread on audit logging requirements: what fields are needed for compliance and incident retros; links to draft ADR.
Thread about monitor staleness and metric lag: how to detect missing data, and what the controller should do (fail-open vs fail-closed).
Thread planning oncall readiness: what pages/alerts will fire, how incident-bot will notify, and who owns first response.
Thread about staged enablement and release checklist; includes discussion of feature flags and rollback plan for the feature.
Thread with PM clarifying MVP: pause vs rollback semantics, per-tier defaults, and how it should appear in Console.
Thread coordinating PR sequencing across repos (redwood + slo-toolkit + observability-pack) and how to avoid breaking changes.
Thread on dashboard requirements and alert routing: which alerts should page vs notify, and how to tag rollout ids for investigation.
Thread for an incident-like simulation: latency spike during canary; team observes whether auto-pause triggers and discusses gaps.
Thread collecting post-game-day findings: false positives, missing monitors, and follow-up tasks to harden suppression and audit trails.
Thread discussing policy engine validation edge cases (bad configs, unsafe thresholds) and what error messages should look like.
Thread on operational ownership: who gets paged for auto-rollback events (SRE vs service owner) and how to handle multi-tenant impact.
Thread reviewing E2E test plan and synthetic signal injection; QA + engineers align on staging setup.
Thread after first staging rollout: status updates, small bug triage, and decision to expand to one internal production route.
Thread about alert noise: tuning thresholds and adding suppression during known telemetry outages; includes quick patch suggestions.
Thread announcing internal availability of auto-rollback (behind flag), with doc links and instructions for service teams to opt in.

Customer support ticket reporting latency regression during model rollout; includes timeline, affected regions, and request for auto-rollback capability; links to Slack incident thread and dashboards.
Support ticket: customer saw 5xx spike during A/B test; asks for configurable rollback thresholds and visibility into rollback decisions.
Internal helpdesk ticket: request to update RBAC permissions so only specific admins can set suppression/override; includes approvals and auditing requirements.
Internal support ticket: oncall users missing access to new dashboards; request to update access groups and document the process.

Transcript of a technical deep dive with an enterprise prospect/customer asking for SLO-based rollback during model rollouts; captures requirements (latency/error thresholds, audit trail, override controls) that feed the PRD.

CRM company record for a customer/prospect with strict latency SLA needs; notes include desire for automated rollback on SLO breach, linked call transcript id, and any related support escalation keys.
Email thread among internal stakeholders (PM + Eng + SRE) confirming MVP scope, success metrics, and launch gating checklist; references Confluence PRD and Linear project.
Email thread for SRE sign-off: paging rules, dashboard readiness, runbook completion, and criteria to enable auto-rollback for production services.
Release engineering email thread coordinating the release train: feature flag defaults, staged enablement schedule, and backout instructions if issues appear.
